html:
A dynasty founded by the Tuoba clan of the Xianbei that ruled north China from 386 to 535. The map shows it in 500, near its height.

The Tuoba began as steppe chiefs in northern Shanxi and by 439 had united all of north China, ending the Sixteen Kingdoms. Across the Huai River they faced a line of southern Chinese dynasties.

Northern Wei rulers made Buddhism a pillar of the state and carved the great cave temples of Yungang and Longmen. The equal-field system they began, which gave each household land to farm, lasted into the Tang. Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang in 494 and ordered the Xianbei elite to take Chinese names, dress and speech.

The frontier armies resented these changes and rebelled in the 520s, and in 534 and 535 the state split into Eastern and Western Wei. Families from the old Northern Wei frontier went on to found the Sui and Tang.
sum: A dynasty founded by the Tuoba clan of the Xianbei that ruled north China from 386 to 535. The map shows it in 500, near its height.
